newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch-Norwegian electricity link moves closer.
newsitem.headline: Dutch-Norwegian electricity link moves closer.

text.p: The Netherlands officially opened an electricity line on Thursday which will eventually let it tap into Norwegian hydro-electricity, the electricity producers association said.

The 145-km high voltage line links Zwolle in the central Netherlands with Eemshaven on the north coast, ostensibly to reach the 1,675 megawatt gas-fired Eemscentrale power plant, completed earlier this year.
However, it is also a further step in the widening of the European electricity network.

"In 2001, there will be a sea-link between Norway and Holland and we will then be importing 600 MW of hydro- electricity. It also improves our links with Germany," said a spokeswoman for Sep, the umbrella association for Dutch electricity producers.
She said there were no plans to feed electricity along the line from Norway to other European countries.
The line was built at a cost of 700 million guilders and came into operation in May.
